plugins.name: vscode-debug
plugins.description: Place real VS Code / Cursor breakpoints from the terminal — the red dots in the gutter, not injected breakpoint() calls — and turn a command that works into a steppable walkthrough of the code.

plugins.name: kiss-rules
plugins.description: KISS rules, injected into every session: keep code simple and stupid, never commit unless asked, no authorship trailers in commit messages, and artifacts visual, not verbose.

plugins.name: user-sleep
plugins.description: Tell the agent you are going to sleep: from then on it asks nothing and blocks on nothing — it makes best-judgment decisions, keeps working, and leaves a decision log to review in the morning.

plugins.name: reproduce
plugins.description: Point it at a GitHub repo or project page and it gets the code running: clone, short-named env, the biggest model that fits the free GPU memory, at least three verified demos, and a flow artifact where the real examples ride through the flowchart.

plugins.name: paper-explain
plugins.description: Paste a paper link: it files the PDF into your project library, crops the authors' figures, and writes a visual explainer (the problem shown on one running example, then big picture, stages and details), published as a page of one shared artifact and synced to the library's GitHub repo.
